question:
With reference to the Union Cabinet's decision of September 2026 on the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), consider the following statements:
1. The wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage was raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month.
2. The wage ceiling had last been revised in September 2014.
3. The decision applies only to the Employees' Provident Fund and does not extend to the Employees' Pension Scheme or the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Cabinet on 16 September 2026 raised the mandatory-coverage wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, effective 17 September 2026, bringing over 51 lakh additional employees into the net; the ceiling had last been revised in September 2014. Statement 3 is wrong: the enhancement expands access to EPF, EPS (1995) and EDLI (1976) alike. Annual Government outgo is estimated at about Rs 11,339 crore against existing support of about Rs 10,250 crore.
subject: Economy
theme: Social security and formalisation of employment
micro_topic: EPFO wage ceiling raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, approved by Union Cabinet 16 September 2026 and effective 17 September 2026 (Vishwakarma Jayanti); 51 lakh+ additional employees covered; annual outgo about Rs 11,339 crore against existing Rs 10,250 crore and about Rs 56,696 crore over five years; recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee on 16 June 2026; ceiling last revised September 2014; EPF & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952; EPF, EPS 1995 and EDLI 1976; about 7.98 crore contributing members and about 82 lakh EPS pensioners

question: The Supreme Court judgment in Hari Dutta Sharma v. State of U.P. & Ors. (2026), recently in the news, is best described as a ruling concerning which one of the following?
options: (a) The constitutional validity of the SARFAESI Act, 2002 in its application to agricultural land
(b) Unlawful repossession of a hypothecated vehicle by a financier, and the Reserve Bank of India's duty to enforce its own loan-recovery guidelines
(c) The power of the Reserve Bank of India to prohibit banks from providing services to cryptocurrency exchanges
(d) The applicability of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 to personal guarantors of corporate debtors
explanation: In Hari Dutta Sharma v. State of U.P. & Ors. (Neutral Citation 2026 INSC 998), a Bench of Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held that seizing a borrower's truck at about 1 a.m. by breaking the steering lock, without the contractually required seven-day notice and without a signed possession memorandum, arbitrarily deprived him of his livelihood in violation of Articles 14 and 21. The Court awarded Rs 10 lakh compensation, refund of the Rs 4.50 lakh sale price with 6% interest and Rs 50,000 costs, and directed the RBI to secure genuine compliance by NBFCs and scheduled commercial banks with guidelines that it said had 'existed only on paper'.
subject: Polity & Governance
micro_topic: Hari Dutta Sharma v. State of U.P. & Ors., 2026 INSC 998, decided 16 September 2026 by Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe; unlawful night-time repossession of a hypothecated truck by Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd.; violation of Articles 14 and 21 and the right to livelihood; Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 giving RBI directions statutory force; Internet and Mobile Association of India v. RBI (2020); ICICI Bank Ltd. v. Prakash Kaur (2007); Orix Auto Finance v. Jagmander Singh (2006); Sundaram Finance v. T. Thankam (2015); RBI Fair Practices Code and recovery-agent master circulars

question:
With reference to the India Meteorological Department's announcement of September 2026 on the southwest monsoon, consider the following statements:
1. The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon normally begins from extreme north-west India.
2. Cumulative rainfall between 1 June and 13 September 2026 was above the long-period average for the country as a whole.
3. Among the broad homogeneous regions, the South Peninsula recorded the largest rainfall deficiency in the 2026 season up to mid-September.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. IMD said on 14 September 2026 that conditions were becoming favourable for withdrawal from parts of West Rajasthan around 19 September, about two days after the normal date of 17 September; withdrawal always begins from extreme north-west India and proceeds south-eastward, clearing the mainland by around 15 October. The South Peninsula was worst hit at 28% below normal. Statement 2 is wrong: all-India rainfall from 1 June to 13 September 2026 was 15% BELOW normal.
subject: Geography
theme: Indian monsoon — onset, withdrawal and rainfall variability
micro_topic: IMD statement of 14 September 2026 on withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from parts of West Rajasthan around 19 September 2026 against a normal date of 17 September; season rainfall 1 June to 13 September 2026 at 15% below normal; South Peninsula -28%, East and North-East India -25%, North-West India -10%, Central India -6%; June -36.5% and July +1%; kharif acreage as on 11 September about 1.45% below last year and 0.72% below the five-year normal; reservoir storage 129.87 BCM in 178 reservoirs against 159.18 BCM last year and a ten-year average of 134.23 BCM

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the case relating to the Jhiram Ghati attack of 2013, in which a special court pronounced sentence in September 2026:
1. The case was investigated by the National Investigation Agency, which was constituted under an Act of Parliament passed in 2008.
2. A death sentence awarded by such a special court can be carried out only after it is confirmed by the High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Both are correct. The NIA Special Court at Jagdalpur sentenced all ten convicts to death on 16 September 2026 for the 25 May 2013 CPI (Maoist) ambush on the Congress 'Parivartan Yatra' convoy at Jhiram Ghati, Darbha, Bastar district, in which 24 people died on the spot and the toll rose further as the injured succumbed. The NIA was constituted under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008, enacted after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks. A death sentence passed at the sessions level must be confirmed by the High Court before it can be executed; the convicts were also given 30 days to appeal.
subject: Internal Security
micro_topic: Jhiram Ghati (Jhiram Valley) attack of 25 May 2013 at Darbha, Bastar district, Chhattisgarh on the Congress Parivartan Yatra convoy; 24 killed on the spot including Mahendra Karma and Nand Kumar Patel, with former Union Minister V. C. Shukla among those who died later; conviction on 5 September 2026 and death sentence for all 10 on 16 September 2026 by the NIA Special Court, Jagdalpur; charges under IPC, Arms Act 1959, Explosive Substances Act 1908 and UAPA 1967; 101 prosecution witnesses; 39 originally chargesheeted; High Court confirmation required for death sentence; NIA Act 2008 and its 2019 amendment; CPI (Maoist) Tactical Counter Offensive Campaign

question:
With reference to the PM Vishwakarma scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented on a cost-sharing basis between the Centre and the States.
2. It provides collateral-free enterprise development loans in two tranches at a concessional rate of interest.
3. Barbers, washermen and garland makers are among the trades eligible under the scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. PM Vishwakarma offers collateral-free 'Enterprise Development Loans' of Rs 1 lakh (first tranche, 18 months) and Rs 2 lakh (second tranche, 30 months) at a concessional 5% interest with Government interest subvention of up to 8%; barbers (naai), washermen (dhobi) and garland makers (malakaar) are among the 18 eligible trades. Statement 1 is wrong: it is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by the Centre, with an outlay of Rs 13,000 crore under the Ministry of MSME. On its third anniversary on 17 September 2026 it reported meeting its 30 lakh registration target.
subject: Society
theme: Welfare schemes for artisans and the informal sector
micro_topic: PM Vishwakarma launched 17 September 2023, Central Sector Scheme with Rs 13,000 crore outlay under the Ministry of MSME with the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and the Department of Financial Services; 18 trades including carpenter, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, cobbler, mason, barber, washerman, garland maker and tailor; recognition via certificate and ID; basic training 5-7 days and advanced training 15 days with Rs 500 per day stipend; toolkit incentive up to Rs 15,000 via e-RUPI; collateral-free loans of Rs 1 lakh and Rs 2 lakh at 5% with up to 8% interest subvention; Rs 1 per digital transaction incentive; third anniversary 17 September 2026 with 30 lakh registered, 24.37 lakh trained, 18.16 lakh toolkits and 6.19 lakh loans worth about Rs 5,316 crore

question:
With reference to the right to livelihood under the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court in Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985) held that the right to livelihood is an integral part of the right to life under Article 21.
2. Article 41 directs the State to make effective provision for securing the right to work, within the limits of its economic capacity and development.
3. The protection of Article 21 is available only to citizens of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Olga Tellis (1985) read the right to livelihood into the right to life under Article 21, reasoning that no person can live without the means of living. Article 41 is the Directive Principle on the right to work, to education and to public assistance, expressly subject to the State's economic capacity and development. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 21 uses the word 'person', so its protection extends to citizens and non-citizens alike, unlike Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30, which are available only to citizens.
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Fundamental Rights — Article 21 and its expanding scope
micro_topic: Right to livelihood as part of Article 21; Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985); Article 41 Directive Principle on right to work, education and public assistance; Article 21 available to all persons including non-citizens; the Article 21 expansion line from Maneka Gandhi (1978) through Francis Coralie Mullin and Olga Tellis to Puttaswamy (2017)

question:
With reference to the retreating or north-east monsoon season in India, consider the following statements:
1. The retreat of the southwest monsoon is a more gradual process than its onset.
2. During October to December, the north-east monsoon brings the bulk of the annual rainfall to the Coromandel Coast.
3. The retreating monsoon season in India is associated with the formation of tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: All three are correct. The onset of the southwest monsoon is abrupt (the monsoon 'burst'), whereas the retreat is gradual, beginning from extreme north-west India around 17 September and clearing the mainland by about 15 October. As the winds reverse, the north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and delivers the bulk of the annual rainfall to the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra Pradesh, along with Rayalaseema and south interior Karnataka, in October to December. October and November are also peak months for tropical cyclogenesis over the Bay of Bengal, aided by the southward shift of the ITCZ and high sea-surface temperatures.
subject: Geography
theme: Indian climate — seasons and the north-east monsoon
micro_topic: Retreating monsoon season October to November; gradual withdrawal from mid-September to mid-October contrasted with the abrupt monsoon burst at onset; October heat as high temperature with high humidity; north-east monsoon rainfall over the Coromandel Coast, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Kerala in October to December; southward shift of the ITCZ; Bay of Bengal tropical cyclones peaking in October and November
